prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t name one absolute “best” roofer for hail damage in Denver (that depends on your location, roof type, insurance situation and timing), but I can help you find the right contractor and avoid common problems. Here’s a practical plan you can use right away — and if you want, share your ZIP code and I’ll suggest several top-rated local contractors you can contact.

How to pick the right hail-damage roofer
- Check credentials
  - Proper Colorado license/registration and general liability + workers’ comp insurance.
  - Local physical address and established local presence (not a storm-chaser).
- Experience with insurance claims
  - Look for contractors who regularly work with homeowners and adjusters and will document damage for your insurer (photos, measurements, Xactimate-style estimates).
- Reviews and references
  - Read recent Google, Yelp, Angi and BBB reviews; ask for 3 local references for recent hail repairs.
- Written, detailed estimate
  - Must list materials, shingle brand & class (impact-resistant options), tear-off vs. overlay, removal of old materials, permits, timeline, cleanup and total cost.
- Warranties
  - Manufacturer shingle warranty (ask what is transferable) and a workmanship warranty from the contractor (in writing).
- Quality materials & code compliance
  - Ask about Class 3/4 impact-rated shingles if desired, proper underlayment, flashing, ventilation, and that they will pull permits and meet local code.

Key questions to ask any roofer
1. Are you licensed and insured? Can you provide copies?
2. How many hail-damage roofs have you repaired in the Denver area?
3. Do you handle the insurance claim or work directly with adjusters?
4. Will you provide a written, line-item estimate and photos of damage?
5. What brand/type of shingles and warranties will be used?
6. Who will supervise and who does the actual work (employees vs subcontractors)?
7. Do you pull permits and provide lien waivers on final payment?
8. What is your cleanup policy and timeline for completion?

Warning signs / red flags
- Contractors who pressure you to sign immediately or require large cash-only deposits.
- “Storm chasers” with out-of-town vans, no local address, no local references.
- No written estimate, vague pricing, or refusal to provide proof of insurance.
- Offers to waive your deductible (that’s illegal and can get you and the contractor in trouble).

Where to search for reputable roofers
- Google Maps (look for companies with many recent reviews)
- Angi, Yelp and HomeAdvisor
- BBB for complaints
- Colorado Roofing Contractors Association or local trade groups
- Ask your insurance company for preferred contractors (but get independent estimates too)

If you want, I can:
- Suggest a short list of highly rated Denver roofers if you provide your ZIP code (I’ll recommend how to vet each).
- Review estimates or contract language you receive (paste them here) and point out anything you should negotiate or clarify.

Tell me your ZIP code or paste any estimates/contracts and I’ll help you next.
